title: Physical quantities and their units
competency: Distinguish between fundamental and derived quantities and their SI units.

keywords.def: A property of an object that can be measured, or calculated from other physical quantities.
The known fixed quantity a measurement is compared with, like the metre or the kilogram.
The International System of Units, used all over the world.
A quantity that cannot be expressed in terms of any other quantity, like length, mass, time and temperature.
A quantity that depends on one or more fundamental quantities, like area, volume, speed and density.

en.text: A physical quantity is anything we can measure, like length, mass, time or temperature. Every measurement has two parts: a number and a unit. "32 kg" means the number 32 and the unit kilogram. The SI is the system of units used all over the world.

am.text: ፊዚካዊ መጠን ሊለካ የሚችል ነገር ነው፤ ርዝመት፣ መጠነ ቁስ፣ ጊዜ፣ ሙቀት። እያንዳንዱ ልኬት ቁጥርና መለኪያ አሐድ አለው፤ 32 ኪ.ግ።

screens.title: 32 what?
screens.ask: Selam says, "My mass is 32." What is missing?
screens.after: The unit. 32 what? 32 kg is very different from 32 g. A measurement needs a number AND a unit.

screens.title: Physical quantities
paras: We measure vegetables' mass, liquids' volume, a car's speed and the day's temperature.
Quantities that can be measured are called physical quantities.
Examples: length, mass, time, temperature, area, volume, density, force.

screens.title: Number and unit
paras: Measurement compares an unknown quantity with a known one.
The known fixed quantity is called a unit.
A student's mass of 32 kg: the quantity is mass, the value is 32, the unit is kilogram (kg).
screens.note: The SI (International System of Units) is used all over the world.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A property of an object that can be measured, or calculated from other physical quantities.
The known fixed quantity a measurement is compared with, like the metre or the kilogram.
The International System of Units, used all over the world.

screens.text: Number and unit: in "the road is 5 km long", what is the unit?
screens.why:
A measurement has a number and a unit.
The number tells how many: 5.
The unit tells what we counted: km (kilometre).
So the unit is km.
"Road" and "long" are just words in the sentence.
screens.clue: The unit tells you what you counted.

screens.text: Physical quantities: which of these can be measured with an instrument?
screens.why:
A physical quantity can be measured.
Length: a ruler. Mass: a balance.
Temperature: a thermometer. Time: a clock.
Kindness and beauty have no instrument and no unit.
So they are not physical quantities.
screens.clue: Can you measure it with an instrument?

screens.text: Parts of a measurement, true or false: every measurement has two parts, a number and a unit.
screens.why:
Look at 32 kg.
The number (magnitude) is 32.
The unit is kg.
Without both parts the measurement is not complete.
So it is true.

screens.title: Number or unit?
screens.text: Parts of a measurement: sort each part into number or unit.
screens.why:
The number tells how many.
32, 5 and 1.6 are numbers.
The unit tells what was counted.
kg (kilogram), km (kilometre) and s (second) are units.
A full measurement needs both, like 32 kg.
screens.clue: Does it say how many, or what was counted?

screens.text: Why units matter: Dawit writes his height as "150". Mekdes writes hers as "1.6". Who is taller?
opts: You cannot tell without the units
screens.ans: You cannot tell without the units
screens.why:
The numbers have no units.
If Dawit means 150 cm, he is 1.5 m tall.
If Mekdes means 1.6 m, she is taller.
But the numbers could mean other units.
Without units we cannot compare. So you cannot tell.

en.text: Fundamental quantities cannot be expressed through other quantities: length (m), mass (kg), time (s) and temperature (K). Derived quantities are built from them: area = m × m = m², volume = m³, speed = m/s, density = kg/m³.

am.text: መሠረታዊ መጠኖች በሌላ መጠን አይገለጹም፤ ርዝመት (ሜ)፣ መጠነ ቁስ (ኪ.ግ)፣ ጊዜ (ሰ)፣ ሙቀት (K)። ተዛማጅ መጠኖች ከእነሱ ይገነባሉ፤ ስፋት ሜ²፣ ይዘት ሜ³፣ ፍጥነት ሜ/ሰ።

screens.title: Basic or built?
screens.text: Before you read, guess: which quantities stand alone?
items: Length is not made from other quantities.

screens.title: Fundamental quantities
paras: Fundamental (base) quantities cannot be expressed in terms of any other quantity.
There are seven: length, mass, time, temperature, electric current, luminous intensity and amount of substance.
Their units are fundamental units. Tap each one below to see its SI unit.

screens.title: Table 1.1: the seven fundamental quantities
screens.ask: Tap each quantity to see its SI unit and symbol.
items: How bright a light is. SI unit: candela. Symbol: cd.

screens.title: Derived quantities
paras: Derived quantities depend on one or more fundamental quantities.
Their units combine base units by multiplying, dividing or powering.

screens.title: Build derived units from metres
screens.note: Length, width and height are fundamental: they are in metres. Area and volume are derived: m × m = m² and m × m × m = m³.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A quantity that cannot be expressed in terms of any other quantity, like length, mass, time and temperature.
A quantity that depends on one or more fundamental quantities, like area, volume, speed and density.

screens.title: Example 1.1: units of area and speed
steps: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
Both are lengths, measured in metres.
So the unit of area = m × m = m².
Distance is in m and time in s, so the unit of speed = m/s.

screens.text: Fundamental quantities: which one is fundamental?
screens.why:
There are seven fundamental quantities, like length, mass, time and temperature.
Temperature is on that list.
Area = length × width, so area is derived.
Volume and force are also built from others.
So the answer is temperature.
screens.clue: Which one is not built from others?

screens.text: Derived units: the SI unit of density is
screens.why:
Density = mass ÷ volume.
The unit of mass is kg.
The unit of volume is m³.
Divide the units: kg ÷ m³ = kg/m³.
kg/m² would be mass per area, not per volume.
screens.clue: Density is mass divided by volume.

screens.text: SI units: match each quantity with its SI unit.
screens.why:
Mass is fundamental: kilogram, kg.
Temperature is fundamental: kelvin, K.
Area = m × m = m².
Volume = m × m × m = m³.
Density = kg ÷ m³ = kg/m³.
screens.clue: Area is square metres; volume is cubic metres.

screens.ask: Unit of volume: volume = length × width × height, so its unit is m × m × m = ___
screens.why:
Length, width and height are all lengths.
Each is measured in metres, m.
m × m × m = m³ (cubic metre).
So the unit of volume is m³.

screens.text: Fundamental or derived? Pressure is force ÷ area. Which kind of quantity is pressure?
opts: Derived, because it is made from other quantities
Fundamental, because it has a unit
screens.ans: Derived, because it is made from other quantities
screens.why:
Pressure is made by dividing force by area.
Area is built from length.
Force is built from mass, length and time.
Anything built from other quantities is derived.
So pressure is derived. Having a unit does not make it fundamental.
screens.clue: Is it built from other quantities?

items.ask: Unit of density: density = mass ÷ volume. Its unit = kg ÷ m³ = ___
items.why:
Density = mass ÷ volume.
The unit of mass is kg.
The unit of volume is m³.
Divide the units: kg ÷ m³ = kg/m³.
items.clue: Divide the mass unit by the volume unit.

items.text: Unit of force: force = mass × acceleration. Its unit is
items.why:
The unit of mass is kg.
Acceleration is change of speed per second: (m/s) ÷ s = m/s².
Multiply: kg × m/s² = kg·m/s².
This unit is called the newton (N).
m/s is the unit of speed; kg/m³ is density.

test.text: Derived quantities: which one is derived?
test.why:
A derived quantity is built from others.
Area = length × width.
So area is derived.
Mass, time and length are fundamental.

test.text: SI units: the SI unit of time is
test.why:
Time is a fundamental quantity.
Its SI unit is the second, symbol s.
Minutes, hours and days are bigger units made of seconds.
So the answer is second.

Derived quantities are built from fundamental quantities.
So their units are built from fundamental units.
Examples: m × m = m², m ÷ s = m/s.
So derived units are made by combining fundamental units.

test.ask: SI units: the SI unit of volume is ___
test.why:
Volume = length × width × height.
Each length is in metres.
m × m × m = m³.
So the SI unit of volume is m³ (cubic metre).

test.text: Unit of speed: speed = distance ÷ time. Its unit is
test.why:
Distance is in metres, m.
Time is in seconds, s.
Divide: m ÷ s = m/s.
s/m is upside down, so it is wrong.
